newsitem.title: FINLAND: Helsinki takes breather ahead of Motorola Q4.
newsitem.headline: Helsinki takes breather ahead of Motorola Q4.

text.p: Shares took a breather on Thursday, easing in slower volumes after Wednesday's spurt but ending off earlier lows as Nokia picked up late on ahead of its U.S. rival Motorola's fourth quarter report.
The HEX index dipped 0.11 percent to 2,613.87 with volume at about 500 million markka well down on Wednesday's bumper level but still solid for Helsinki.
Underlying sentiment remained strong but there were fears of near-term volatility, brokers said.
"There was a clear positive tone," one said, noting Nokia traded above its close in New York most of the day.
In the U.S., Motorola was expected to report lower earnings after the New York close and analysts said they would be looking for any hints of a rebound in semiconductors and mobile phones.
Forestry shares pared Wednesday's strong gains, but UPM made a late come-back to close at 99.20, off just 0.30 markka.
"We might have been too bullish yesterday," one broker said.

Brokers said both foreign and domestic investors were in the market and the "January effect" continued to play a supporting role. "There is so much money in this market that small investors are also out there," said one.
Raisio was among the top risers, adding 7.00 markka to 310.00 in lively trade as brokers said investors rediscovered the stock.
The International Herald Tribune newspaper published a story on Raisio which quoted an analyst as saying that its Benecol cholesterol-reducing product was "more significant than Nutrasweet".
Information technology group TT Tieto was lively, falling 2.3 percent or 10 markka to 430.00 in what one broker called a correction to gains of over 10 percent already this year.
